tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary:
Fixed `money.Amount.Decimal()` in `money/amount.go` to format amounts using the currency's `Exponent` and `Factor()` rather than assuming 2 decimal places (`m/100`, `%02d`):
- Zero-decimal currencies (CLP, JPY; `Exponent == 0`) render as integers with no decimal point (e.g. `"15000"`, `"0"`, `"-15000"`).
- Positive-exponent currencies (USD/EUR/BRL/... with 2 decimals, KWD with 3 decimals) render with `Exponent` zero-padded fractional digits (`%0*d`), preserving minus signs on negative amounts (including sub-unit negative amounts and `math.MinInt64`).
- Added unit tests in `money/money_test.go` and end-to-end API tests in `api/api_test.go` covering CLP, JPY, and KWD create, get, list, fee, and refund responses.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4420 in `payment.Service.Refund` by checking the requested refund amount against `p.Remaining().Minor` instead of `p.Amount.Minor`. Refunds exceeding the remaining refundable balance are now rejected with `ErrRefundExceedsRemaining` (HTTP 422 `refund_exceeds_remaining`) without modifying the payment, while refunding the exact remaining balance succeeds and transitions the payment to `REFUNDED`. Added unit and HTTP API tests covering partial refunds, over-refund rejections, exact remaining refunds, and concurrent refunds.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary: Fixed an off-by-one bug in cursor pagination (`store.Memory.ListByMerchant`): `encodeCursor(end)` already encodes the start offset of the next page, so incrementing the decoded `offset` (`offset++`) skipped the first item of every page after the first. Removed the erroneous `offset++` and added tests in `store` and `api` verifying full-page walking across all page sizes and item counts (including exact multiples of `limit` and `limit=1`).

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
Fixed webhook retry classification in `webhook/dispatcher.go` (`retryable`):
- Changed status range check from `status >= 400 && status < 500` to `status >= 500 && status < 600` so transport errors, 408, 429, and 5xx responses are retried with exponential backoff up to `MaxAttempts`, while permanent non-2xx responses (such as 3xx and other 4xx like 400/401/404/410) go straight to the dead-letter list after a single attempt with `Attempts` and `LastStatus` recorded.
- Guarded `deliver` against context cancellation before/during `Send` so canceled deliveries stay queued rather than being dead-lettered, and normalized `MaxAttempts` to at least 1.
- Added unit tests in `webhook/webhook_test.go` covering permanent failures, transient status retries, retry exhaustion into dead letters, and transient-to-permanent transitions.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary:
Fixed idempotency key TTL expiry and memory eviction in `idempotency.Memory`:

- Updated `Memory.purgeLocked` to evict records once `!now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)` (`now >= ExpiresAt`) instead of `now.Sub(r.ExpiresAt) > m.ttl`, which was doubling the effective TTL to 48h and using a strict inequality.
- Updated `Memory.Begin` to check `now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)` on lookup so expired keys immediately behave as unused (starting a new request regardless of fingerprint or prior completion state) even between throttled purge intervals.
- Updated `Memory.Complete` and `Memory.Release` to treat expired keys (`!now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)`) as unknown (`ErrUnknownKey`) and remove them from the map.
- Added unit and API tests covering TTL boundary behavior, fingerprint reuse after expiry, in-progress expiry, eviction via `Len()`, concurrency, and end-to-end payment creation after TTL expiry.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary:
Fixed integer overflow in `webhook.Policy.Backoff` when computing `BaseDelay * 2^(n-1)` for large attempt numbers (such as enterprise policies with `MaxAttempts: 48`, where `time.Second << (n-1)` previously overflowed `int64` into negative/zero durations after ~34 attempts and caused immediate back-to-back retries).

Changes:
- `webhook/dispatcher.go`: Updated `Policy.Backoff(n)` to clamp `n <= 1`, guard against non-positive delays, and check `shift >= 63 || p.BaseDelay > p.MaxDelay>>shift` before left-shifting so backoff durations never overflow, never decrease, stay positive, and cap cleanly at `MaxDelay` for any attempt count.
- `webhook/webhook_test.go`: Added unit tests verifying monotonicity, positivity, and `MaxDelay` capping across attempt numbers and policies, plus an end-to-end 48-attempt enterprise retry schedule test.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
Implemented payment cancellation before capture (PAY-4502):

- Added `payment.StatusCanceled` (`"CANCELED"`), marked it as final in `Status.Final()`, and registered it in `allStatuses` for case-insensitive parsing via `ParseStatus`.
- Added `(*payment.Service).Cancel(ctx context.Context, id string) (Payment, error)` allowing transitions from `CREATED` and `PENDING` to `CANCELED`, emitting the `"payment.canceled"` event, and returning wrapped `ErrInvalidTransition` or `ErrNotFound` errors otherwise.
- Added HTTP endpoint `POST /payments/{id}/cancel` returning `200 OK` with the canceled payment, `409 invalid_transition` when not cancelable, and `404 not_found` for unknown IDs.
- Added unit and HTTP/webhook tests covering status parsing/finality, valid and invalid cancel transitions, terminal state enforcement (409 on authorize, capture, decline, refund, or repeat cancel), and webhook event delivery.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary: Added `CanTransition(from, to Status) bool` in `payment/payment.go` as the single source of truth for allowed payment status transitions (`CREATED->PENDING`, `CREATED->DECLINED`, `PENDING->SUCCEEDED`, `PENDING->DECLINED`, `SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED`) and derived `Status.Final()` from it. Refactored `Service.Authorize`, `Service.Capture`, `Service.Decline`, and `Service.Refund` in `payment/service.go` to validate transitions exclusively via `CanTransition` without status switches/chains, preserving all existing public behavior, events, and wrapped errors. Added unit tests covering `CanTransition` and `Status.Final()`.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
Fixed concurrency bugs and data races in `idempotency.Memory`:

- Held `Memory.mu` across the entire check-and-insert critical section in `Begin` (including record inspection and `copyRecord`), preventing TOCTOU races where concurrent retries for the same `Idempotency-Key` could both start execution and create duplicate operations (such as duplicate refunds), as well as preventing data races on `*Record` fields.
- Protected map lookups and record updates in `Complete` and `Release` with `Memory.mu`, eliminating `concurrent map read and map write` crashes and data races under concurrent traffic.
- Added concurrent unit tests in `idempotency/store_test.go` and a concurrent idempotent refund retry integration test in `api/api_test.go`.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
Fixed data races and phantom refunds caused by shared `Payment.Refunds` slice backing arrays across `store.Memory` and `payment.Service`:

- **`store.Memory` (`store/memory.go`)**: Deep-copy `payment.Payment` via `p.Clone()` in `Create`, `Get`, `Update`, and `ListByMerchant` so values passed to or returned by the repository never share mutable `Refunds` slice state (including spare slice capacity) with stored payments. Previously, concurrent `Get` + `append` calls mutated the stored `Refunds` backing array in place when spare capacity existed, causing a data race and leaving phantom refund entries from version-conflicted requests in the stored payment.
- **`payment.Payment.Clone` (`payment/payment.go`)**: Allocate an exact-capacity slice (`make([]Refund, len(p.Refunds))` + `copy`) when `p.Refunds != nil`, preserving `nil` vs empty non-nil slices while eliminating any shared backing array or excess capacity.
- **`payment.Service` (`payment/service.go`)**: Clone `Payment` across repository boundaries and event publication in `Create`, `Get`, `List`, and `mutate` while preserving existing optimistic locking semantics.
- **Tests (`store/memory_test.go`, `payment/service_test.go`)**: Added unit and concurrent `-race` tests covering slice isolation across `Create`/`Get`/`Update`/`ListByMerchant`, `Payment.Clone`, concurrent refund waves, and version-conflicted refunds when `Refunds` has spare capacity.

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
Fixed O(N log N) per-request eviction overhead in `idempotency.(*Memory).Begin` (PAY-4570).

Root cause:
`(*Memory).Begin` called `purgeLocked` on every request, copying all stored records from `m.records` into a slice and sorting them by `ExpiresAt` (`O(N log N)` CPU and `O(N)` allocations per `Begin` call), causing POST latency on `/payments` and `/payments/{id}/refunds` to grow superlinearly as live idempotency keys accumulated.

Changes:
- Maintained an intrusive doubly-linked list of entries ordered by `ExpiresAt` alongside `m.records` in `idempotency/store.go`.
- `purgeLocked` now pops expired entries from the head of the list in `O(1)` per expired key (and `O(1)` single-pointer check with zero allocations when the oldest key is still live).
- `insertLocked` appends new keys to the tail in `O(1)` (with fallback insertion if the clock ever moves backwards), and `removeLocked` unlinks entries in `O(1)` on `Release`, expiry eviction, or expired-key overwrite.
- Added unit, concurrency, expiry/eviction, and 50k-live-key latency tests in `idempotency/store_test.go`.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
Replaced floating-point independent rounding in `money.Allocate` with exact integer Largest Remainder allocation (`math/bits` 128-bit arithmetic with a `math/big` fallback when the sum of ratios overflows `uint64`).

Changes:
- `money/allocate.go`: Compute floored proportional shares and exact integer remainders without floating point or overflow, then distribute leftover minor units one each to the indices with the largest fractional remainders (breaking ties by lower index) so parts always sum to `a` and stay within 1 minor unit of their exact share.
- `money/money_test.go`: Added unit and property-based tests covering the reported marketplace split scenarios, tie-breaking, zero amounts/ratios, multi-exponent currencies, integer overflow boundaries, and randomized contract verification against `math/big.Rat`.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
Replaced raw HTTP body hashing (`bodyFingerprint`) with canonical semantic request fingerprinting (`requestFingerprint`) in `api/idempotency.go` and `api/handlers.go`.

- `POST /payments` now computes the idempotency fingerprint from the parsed canonical request (`merchant_id`, normalized decimal `amount`, and uppercase ISO `currency` code).
- `POST /payments/{id}/refunds` now computes the idempotency fingerprint from the parsed canonical refund `amount` (including currency).
- Retries that rebuild JSON with different field order, whitespace, string escaping, currency casing, or equivalent decimal amount representations (`"10.50"` vs `"10.5"`, `"5.00"` vs `"5"`) produce the same fingerprint and replay the stored response instead of returning `422 idempotency_key_reused`, while semantically different requests with the same key continue to be rejected with `422`.
- Added unit tests in `api/api_test.go` covering semantic equivalence and conflict detection for payment creation and refund retries.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary:
Fixed `money.Fee` to compute fees using exact overflow-safe integer arithmetic and half-to-even (banker's) rounding instead of `float64` multiplication/division with `math.Ceil`.

- Replaced the `float64` + `math.Ceil` calculation in `money/fee.go` with exact quotient/remainder decomposition modulo 10000 (`a.Minor = q*10000 + r`), avoiding both floating-point precision loss and `int64` overflow across the full `[0, math.MaxInt64]` range, and rounding ties (`.5`) to the nearest even minor unit.
- Added unit and API tests in `money/money_test.go` and `api/api_test.go` covering the `10.05 USD` @ 290 bps case (`0.29`), exact half-to-even tie-breaking across currencies, invalid inputs, and boundary/large `int64` amounts verified against an arbitrary-precision `math/big` oracle.
